title: Polynomial coefficient tensors as a quotient of the coefficient kernel
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $A=P/I$, $Q=P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, and $C$ a commutative $A$-algebra. Let $\alpha:A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C$ be an $A$-algebra map and let $\varphi:Q\to C$ be surjective with $\varphi=\alpha\circ\pi$, where $\pi$ reduces coefficients. Put $H=\ker\pi$ and $J=\ker\varphi$. There exists a $Q$-linear equivalence $e:C\otimes_A(I/I^2)\simeq H/JH$ such that $e(c\otimes[x])=[\widetilde c\operatorname{C}(x)]$, where $\widetilde c$ is the chosen section of $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 00S2, proof of lemma-exact-sequence-NL, coefficient kernel and conormal row; tensor quotient identification as in More on Algebra Tag 07D4, proof of lemma-transitive-lci-at-end

proof.text: Use the coefficient kernel identity H = I Q. The canonical map Q tensor_P I to I Q is injective: after inclusion in Q it is the tensor of the ideal subtype, followed by the tensor unit equivalence, and Q is P-free and hence flat. It is surjective by induction on the ideal span of the constants from I. Thus it is a Q-linear equivalence.

The quotient tensor equivalence gives A tensor_P I = I/I². Extend its scalars from P to A using quotient surjectivity. Apply tensor congruence and cancel the intermediate A to get C tensor_A (I/I²) = C tensor_P I. Tensor the coefficient equivalence with C over Q and cancel Q to identify C tensor_Q H with the same module.

The first isomorphism theorem identifies Q/J with C. Tensor with H and apply the quotient tensor equivalence to obtain C tensor_Q H = H/JH. Compose the preceding equivalences, restricting their scalars from C to Q. On c tensor [x], the first two equivalences give c tensor C(x), and the last gives the class of the chosen section of c times C(x). This proves the formula, including the zero ring and empty variable set.

lean.statement:
theorem polynomial_coefficient_tensor_quotient
    (P : Type u) [CommRing P] (I : Ideal P) (m : ℕ)
    (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [Algebra (P ⧸ I) C]
    (α : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (P ⧸ I) →ₐ[P ⧸ I] C)
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) P →+* C)
    (hφeq : φ = α.toRingHom.comp (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    let E := Extension.ofSurjective φ.toIntAlgHom hφ
    let H := RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m))
    ∃ (e : C ⊗[P ⧸ I] I.Cotangent ≃ₗ[E.Ring]
        H ⧸ (E.ker • (⊤ : Submodule E.Ring H))),
      ∀ (c : C) (x : I) (y : H), y.1 = MvPolynomial.C x.1 →
        e (c ⊗ₜ I.toCotangent x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (E.σ c • y)
